issues.legal_issue: Grounds of preventive detention must be explained in a language the detainee understands so that the right to make a representation can be exercised.
material_facts: The detainee was illiterate and did not understand the written grounds, which were in English.
He swore that the grounds had not been explained to him in a language he understood.

The State relied on an endorsement and a thumb impression as proof of explanation, but the endorsement appeared in different inks, an earlier copy lacked such an endorsement, and the State affidavit had a significant alteration.
The Court preferred the detainee’s account and found that the grounds had not been explained to him in a language he understood.
issues.conclusion: The statutory requirement was not complied with, and the detention was unlawful.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 8 of the Jammu and Kashmir Preventive Detention Act, 1964, grounds must be disclosed to the detainee. When the detainee cannot read or understand the language in which they are supplied, they must be explained as early as possible in a language the detainee understands, so the statutory right to make a representation can be exercised. Merely handing over a document in an alien language and obtaining a thumb impression acknowledging receipt does not satisfy that requirement. The Court relied on the statutory provisions governing detention and disclosure, including sections 3(2), 5 and 8; it identified no earlier case by name on this issue.

predicates.preventive_detention_challenge: The proceeding challenges a person’s preventive detention.
predicates.detenu_cannot_understand_written_grounds: The detainee cannot read or understand the language in which the written grounds are provided.
predicates.grounds_not_explained_in_understood_lang: The grounds are not explained to the detainee in a language the detainee understands.

issues.definition: When a preventive-detention challenge concerns grounds the detainee cannot understand in writing, and those grounds were not explained in a language the detainee understands, the detention is unlawful.

issues.legal_issue: Preventive-detention grounds are impermissibly vague when they omit details needed to make an effective representation.
material_facts: The grounds alleged a conspiracy with unspecified leaders and incitement of landless people to occupy land and resist eviction.
They did not identify the leaders or the people allegedly incited, the dates of the alleged conspiracy or incitement, or when the alleged conference took place.
The Court found it impossible for a person to make a representation against grounds framed without those details.
issues.conclusion: The grounds were vague, so the detention was unlawful.
issues.legal_principle: The grounds disclosed under section 8 of the Jammu and Kashmir Preventive Detention Act, 1964, must be sufficiently precise and detailed to permit an effective representation. Allegations that omit material particulars and thereby make a representation impossible are vague. The Court relied on numerous earlier authorities of the Supreme Court but did not identify them by name, and referred to the Act’s detention provisions, including sections 3(2), 5 and 8.

predicates.preventive_detention_challenge: The proceeding challenges a person’s preventive detention.
predicates.grounds_omit_particulars_needed_for_effe: The grounds omit details needed for the detainee to understand and respond effectively to the allegations.

issues.definition: When a preventive-detention challenge concerns grounds that omit particulars needed for an effective representation, the detention is unlawful.
